questions.question: Define vertical distribution of groundwater.
questions.solution_html:
• Define vertical distribution of groundwater. / [CO1]
  • • Division of subsurface water into two main zones: the Zone of Aeration (Vadose zone) and
  • the Zone of Saturation (Phreatic zone). (1 Mark)
  • • Separated by the Water Table; describes how water occupies voids from the surface down to
  • the impermeable bed. (1 Mark)

questions.question: State the role of GIS in remote sensing.
questions.solution_html:
• State the role of GIS in remote sensing. / [CO2]
  • • GIS acts as a tool for storing and analysing spatial data acquired via remote sensing. (1 Mark)
  • • Allows for overlay analysis (e.g., combining geology and land use maps) to identify potential
  • groundwater zones. (1 Mark)

questions.question: State two limitations of artificial recharge.
questions.solution_html:
• State two limitations of artificial recharge. / [CO4]
  • • Clogging of aquifers (siltation): Silt or microbial growth can reduce permeability at the
  • injection site. (1 Mark)
  • • High initial investment for infrastructure and maintenance. (1 Mark)

questions.question: Describe SP method in the context of surface geophysical method.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe SP method in the context of surface geophysical method. / [CO2]
  • • Principle: Measuring natural potential differences (Self-Potential) in the earth without an
  • artificial current. (2 Marks)
  • • Mechanism: Potentials arise from electrochemical activity or "streaming potential" (water
  • flowing through porous media). (3 Marks)
  • • Application: Useful for locating ore bodies, detecting leaks in dams, or mapping shallow
  • groundwater flow. (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the physical, chemical, and bacteriological standards specified by both WHO guidelines and BIS for potable water quality.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss physical, chemical, and bacteriological standards (WHO & BIS). / [CO3]
  • • Physical: Colour, Odor, turbidity, and taste standards (e.g., Turbidity (2 Marks)
  • • Chemical: Limits for pH (6.5-8.5), Hardness, Iron, and Nitrates. Comparison of BIS (IS 10500)
  • vs. WHO guidelines. (3 Marks)
  • • Bacteriological: Requirement for zero E. coli or coliform counts in 100ml samples for safe
  • potable water. (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the relationship between groundwater overexploitation, hydraulic gradient changes and saline water intrusion in coastal and other aquifers, and describe suitable prevention measures.
questions.solution_html:
• Groundwater overexploitation, hydraulic gradient, and saline water intrusion. / [CO4]
  • • Mechanism: Over-pumping lowers the water table, creating a "cone of depression." [2
  • Marks]
  • • Hydraulic Gradient: Reversal of the gradient causes seawater to flow inland toward the well.
  • (2 Marks)
  • • Saline Intrusion: Ghyben-Herzberg relation (freshwater-saltwater interface). (2 Marks)
  • • Prevention: Controlled pumping, artificial recharge, and creating hydraulic barriers. [2
  • Marks]
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the variations in groundwater quality across different Indian provinces.
questions.solution_html:
• Variations in groundwater quality across Indian provinces. / [CO5]
  • • Arsenic: Dominant in West Bengal and Ganga-Brahmaputra plains. (2 Marks)
  • • Fluoride: High in arid/semi-arid regions like Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Kerala
  • (Palakkad). (2 Marks)
  • • Salinity: Coastal regions (Gujarat/Tamil Nadu) and inland salinity in Punjab/Haryana due to
  • irrigation. (2 Marks)
  • • Iron: Common in North-Eastern states and parts of Kerala/Odisha. (2 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Illustrate how secondary porosity affects water occurrence in hard rocks.
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate how secondary porosity affects water occurrence in hard rocks. / [CO1]
  • • Definition: Porosity created after rock formation via fracturing, jointing, or weathering. [2
  • Marks]
  • • Crystalline Rocks: Igneous/Metamorphic rocks have zero primary porosity; water is stored
  • only in fractures. (3 Marks)
  • • Occurrence: Highly localized; yields depend on fracture connectivity and the thickness of the
  • weathered "saprolite" zone. (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe briefly the various types of sub-surface geophysical method.
questions.solution_html:
• Briefly describe various types of sub-surface geophysical methods. / [CO2]
  • • Borehole Logging: Electrical Resistivity logs (Normal/Lateral) to identify aquifers. (3 Marks)
  • • Gamma Logging: Identifying clay layers vs. sand. (2 Marks)
  • • Sonic/Neutron logging: Measuring porosity and density within the drilled hole. (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain how high SAR values cause soil dispersion and reduced permeability.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how high SAR values cause soil dispersion and reduced permeability. / [CO3]
  • • Definition: Sodium Adsorption Ratio (SAR) measures the ratio of $Na^+$ to $Ca^{2+}$ and
  • $Mg^{2+}$. (2 Marks)
  • • Process: High Sodium replaces Calcium in clay, causing clay particles to swell and disperse. [3
  • Marks]
  • • Impact: Dispersed particles block soil pores, destroying soil structure and drastically reducing
  • permeability/infiltration. (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe radioactive contamination in groundwater and explain the factors influencing its occurrence and distribution. [8x6 = 48]
questions.solution_html:
• Radioactive contamination in groundwater. / [CO4]
  • • Sources: Natural (Radon/Uranium leaching from granitic rocks) and Anthropogenic (Mining,
  • nuclear waste). (3 Marks)
  • • Factors: Geological parent material, pH (solubility), and redox conditions of the aquifer. [3
  • Marks]
  • • Distribution: High concentrations often found in deep fractured aquifers or near mineralized
  • zones. (2 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Categorize groundwater basins and explain the hydrological boundaries that define a basin.
questions.solution_html:
• Categorize groundwater basins and explain hydrological boundaries. / [CO1]
  • • Introduction: Definition of a groundwater basin as a hydrogeologic unit containing one or
  • more aquifers. (2 Marks)
  • • Categories: Open vs. Closed basins; Rock-bounded vs. Alluvial basins. (4 Marks)
  • • Hydrological Boundaries:
  • o Physical: Geological contacts, faults, or impermeable strata. (2 Marks)
  • o Hydraulic: Groundwater divides (crests in water table), streamline boundaries, and
  • constant head boundaries (large rivers/oceans). (4 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the process of liquid waste disposal and explain how it degrades the quality of surrounding groundwater. [12x1 = 12]
questions.solution_html:
• Process of liquid waste disposal and groundwater degradation. / [CO4]
  • • Disposal Methods: Septic tanks, rapid infiltration pits, deep well injection, and lagooning. [4
  • Marks]
  • • Degradation Process: Leaching of pollutants through the vadose zone; formation of a
  • "Contaminant Plume." (4 Marks)
  • • Impacts: Nutrient enrichment (Nitrates), Pathogen introduction, Heavy metal accumulation,
  • and change in pH/Redox chemistry which can trigger further mineral leaching. (4 Marks)
